Samui's one big shopping mall is Central Samui in Chaweng, opposite Chaweng Lake, open daily 10:00–22:00 with more than 200 shops, a department store, a Tops supermarket and a beach-front square; Chaweng Walking Street sets up beside it from Thursday to Saturday. For groceries, the hypermarkets are Lotus's in Bo Phut (08:00–22:00, with a cinema), Big C on the Bophut ring road and two Makro wholesale stores. The AEON ATMs inside Big C and Lotus's charge foreign cards 150 THB per withdrawal, against 220–250 THB at most banks.

Samui is not a shopping destination in the way Bangkok is, but everything you need is here, often at mainland prices in the big stores. This guide covers where to buy what, what it costs, the money and tax rules that save you baht, and the things you shouldn't take home. Hours were checked against 2026 sources; they can change on public holidays.

Central Samui

Central Samui opened on 29 March 2014 as CentralFestival Samui and is run by Central Pattana, Thailand's biggest mall developer. It is the only full-size mall on the island: about 90,000 m² of retail space in a mix of enclosed and open-air wings, with its own stretch of Chaweng Beach behind it.

  • Hours: daily 10:00–22:00; hours can change on Thai public holidays.
  • Address: 209/1-2 Moo 2, Bo Phut, Koh Samui 84320; phone +66 77 962 777.
  • Anchors: Central Department Store, Tops Market, PowerBuy (electronics), SuperSports and B2S (books and stationery), plus more than 200 Thai and international brand shops.
  • Food: a large food court with a market-style section, cafés, juice stalls and sit-down restaurants.
  • Families: a supervised children's play area, clean toilets and air-conditioning.
  • Services: bank branches and exchange counters with longer hours than town branches, phone shops and pharmacies.

The mall's beach-front square is also Samui's main event space. It hosts the free New Year's Eve countdown with concerts and fireworks, a Songkran foam party (13–15 April, 12:00–24:00 in 2025), the Central Samui Neon Run in late May (about 3,000 runners in 2026) and the Samui Open Beach Volleyball in March. Upcoming dates: party and festival calendar.

Supermarkets and hypermarkets

Lotus's Samui

Lotus's (formerly Tesco Lotus) in Bo Phut, on the main road near Chaweng, opens daily 08:00–22:00. It has a large supermarket floor, a low-priced food court (a plate of green curry and rice costs about 135 THB), phone and electronics shops, clothing, the HomePro DIY store, a kids' play area and a cinema. Parking is plentiful and mostly covered.

Big C Supercenter

Big C is on the ring road in Bophut, near Bandon International Hospital. It sells groceries, household goods, clothes and electronics, with smaller shops and an AEON ATM inside. It is the most convenient hypermarket for Bophut, Fisherman's Village and Maenam.

Makro

Two Makro stores stand close together in Bo Phut, near Lotus's: Makro Koh Samui, a warehouse-style wholesale store for groceries and household supplies, and Makro Foodservice, focused on fresh produce, meat and seafood. They are aimed at restaurants but open to everyone, and they are the best place to stock a villa for a group.

Tops, minimarts and fresh markets

Tops Market inside Central Samui has the widest range of imported food, cheese and wine. 7-Eleven and other convenience stores are on every main road, open 24 hours. For fruit, vegetables and fish at local prices, use the fresh markets: Lamai fresh market (about 06:00–20:00) and the morning fish market at Hua Thanon. See Koh Samui markets.

Buying alcohol

Since 29 May 2026, shops, supermarkets and 7-Eleven may sell alcohol from 11:00 to 24:00; the old 14:00–17:00 afternoon ban has ended. On Buddhist holy days, shops can't sell alcohol at all; the 2027 ban days are 21 February, 20 May, 18–19 July and about 15 October, and there are none in November or December 2026. You must be 20 to buy. Wine is heavily taxed in Thailand, so expect to pay more than at home. More: drugs and alcohol law.

Phones and SIM cards

AIS and True both have shops in Central Samui and in the big supermarkets on the ring road. Tourist SIMs with unlimited data cost about 449–499 THB for 8 days, 699 THB for 15 days and 1,199 THB for 30 days in 2026. You need your passport to register a SIM, and the shop staff will set it up for you. eSIMs are sold at the same counters. Chargers, power banks and cables are cheapest at PowerBuy in Central Samui or the electronics shops in Lotus's. Full comparison: SIM cards and Wi-Fi on Koh Samui.

Pharmacies and toiletries

Chain pharmacies and health-and-beauty stores in Central Samui and Lotus's sell sun cream, after-sun, insect repellent, rehydration salts and basic medicines, usually cheaper than beach-road shops. Sun cream is expensive in Thailand compared with Europe, so bring some from home if you can. For prescriptions and a pharmacist's advice, see pharmacies on Koh Samui.

ATMs and money

  • ATM fees: most Thai ATMs charge foreign cards 220–250 THB per withdrawal; the AEON ATMs inside Big C and Lotus's charge 150 THB. Withdraw larger amounts less often to save fees.
  • Decline conversion: when an ATM or card terminal offers to charge you in your home currency, always choose THB. The "guaranteed rate" is worse.
  • Cards: malls and supermarkets take Visa and Mastercard; markets and small shops are cash only.
  • Exchange: bank exchange counters in Central Samui give better rates than hotel desks and keep mall hours.

More: banks, ATMs and money on Koh Samui.

VAT refunds for tourists

Visitors leaving Thailand by air can reclaim the 7 % VAT on goods bought at shops displaying the "VAT Refund for Tourists" sign, such as the department store in Central Samui. In 2026 the rules are:

  • Spend at least 2,000 THB in one shop on one day and ask for the VAT refund form with your passport.
  • Your total claim must reach at least 5,000 THB, and you must leave Thailand within 60 days of purchase.
  • Show the goods, receipts and forms to Customs at the international airport you fly out from, before check-in for goods in your hold luggage, then claim at the refund counter after passport control.
  • A processing fee is deducted, so the net refund is about 5–6 % of the price.

Samui Airport handles VAT refunds for international departures and has offered cash refunds for claims up to 30,000 THB. If you fly Samui to Bangkok and then abroad, you normally claim at your final departure airport, with the goods in your hand luggage. Check the current rules with the Revenue Department's VAT Refund for Tourists office before you rely on a refund.

Tailors, crafts and souvenirs

  • Tailors: Chaweng Beach Road has many tailor shops making suits and dresses in a few days. Quality varies a lot: ask for at least two fittings, see the fabric before you pay a deposit and ignore touts who promise a suit in 24 hours.
  • Crafts: soap carvings, coconut-shell bowls and lamps, sarongs, local art and silver jewellery are best bought at the Friday market in Fisherman's Village and Chaweng Walking Street. See walking streets and Fisherman's Village Walking Street.
  • Food gifts: coconut oil and coconut products, Thai curry pastes, dried fruit and local rum make good gifts. Check your home country's import rules on food and alcohol.
  • Haggling: polite bargaining is normal at markets, never in malls or supermarkets.

What not to buy

  • Vapes and e-cigarettes: illegal in Thailand, including for tourists; possession can bring fines and detention.
  • Counterfeit designer goods: widely sold at markets, but importing them can lead to confiscation and fines in many countries.
  • Coral, shells and starfish: taking them from Thai beaches and parks is illegal, and many countries ban import.
  • Wildlife products: ivory, tortoiseshell, skins and anything from protected species.
  • Cannabis products: buying needs a prescription in Thailand, and taking them home is illegal almost everywhere.

Buddha images and antiques may need an export permit from the Fine Arts Department, other than small amulets worn for worship. [check] Ask the shop for paperwork before you buy anything large or old.

Rainy-day shopping

From late October to December the north-east monsoon brings rainy afternoons to Samui, and November is the wettest month (about 445 mm). Central Samui is the obvious refuge: shops, a food court, cafés and the kids' play area under one roof, with the cinema at Lotus's a short ride away. Combine it with a spa treatment or a cooking class: our small-group Thai cooking class costs 2,000 THB per person. Rain outlook: Koh Samui weather and Koh Samui in November.

Shopping for a villa or a long stay

  • Bulk and fresh food: Makro for meat, seafood, drinks and household basics in quantity.
  • Imported goods: Tops in Central Samui for cheese, cereals and baby food.
  • Home and DIY: HomePro at Lotus's for fans, adaptors, kitchen items and tools.
  • Delivery: food-delivery apps cover Chaweng, Bophut and Lamai, and many supermarkets deliver locally.
  • Drinking water: large refill bottles and water machines are cheaper than buying small bottles.

Planning a longer stay? See Koh Samui villas and where to stay.

Getting to the shops

Central Samui and Lotus's are on or near the ring road in Chaweng and Bo Phut, 10–15 minutes from the airport. Grab works well in this area; a short hop costs about 80–120 THB. Songthaews run along the ring road by day for about 30–80 THB, cash, and mostly stop by 20:00–22:00. All the big stores have free car and scooter parking. See getting around Koh Samui.

A private shopping trip

For groups, families with lots to buy or anyone who wants a translator at the counter, we arrange a private shopping tour by minibus with an English-speaking guide for up to 12 people; message us on WhatsApp for a price.

Shop, then sail

The sea off Samui's south coast is usually calmer than the exposed east coast in the monsoon months, and the Pig Island speedboat tour from Thong Krut (1,450 THB adult, 1,250 THB child) runs every day of the year, including while Ang Thong Marine Park is closed from 1 November to 15 December. Hotel pickup is included from most areas of Koh Samui. All trips: Koh Samui tours.
